current_text.html: Ordination Requirements and Procedures a. An intern applying for ordination shall be required to present a diploma of Bachelor or Master from some approved college or university, and also a diploma of Bachelor or Master from some approved theological seminary or authentic testimonials of having completed a regular course of theological studies, or a certificate of completion of and endorsement from a theological study program as approved by the General Assembly and one of the Presbyteries of the Presbyterian Church in America. No Presbytery shall omit any of these educational requirements except in extraordinary cases, and then only with a three-fourths (3/4) approval of the Presbytery. Whenever a Presbytery shall omit any of these educational requirements, it shall always make a record of the reasons for such omission and the parts omitted. The intern shall also present satisfactory testimonials as to the completion and approval of his internship in the practice of the ministry. b. Every candidate for ordination shall ordinarily have met the requirements of the Assembly's approved curriculum. Ordinarily, the intern shall have been examined in most of the following trials when he was licensed. If the Presbytery previously approved all parts of the licensure examination, it need not re-examine the intern in those areas at this time. If there were areas of weakness, which the Presbytery noted, or if any member of the Presbytery desires to do so, the intern may be examined on particular points again. Additionally, the intern shall be examined on any parts required for ordination which were not covered in his examination for licensure. In all cases, he should be asked to indicate whether he has changed his previous views concerning any points in the Confession of Faith, Catechisms, and Book of Church Order of the Presbyterian Church in America. c. Trials for ordination shall consist of: (1) A careful examination as to: (a) his acquaintance with experiential religion, especially his personal character and family management (based on the qualifications set out in 1 Timothy 3:1-7, and Titus 1:6-9), (b) his knowledge of the Greek and Hebrew languages, (c) Bible content, (d) theology, (e) the Sacraments, (f) Church history, (g) the history of the Presbyterian Church in America, and (h) the principles and rules of the government and discipline of the church. A Presbytery may accept a seminary degree which includes study in the original languages in lieu of an oral examination in the original languages. (2) He shall prepare a thesis on some theological topic assigned by Presbytery. (3) The candidate shall prepare an exegesis on an assigned portion of Scripture, requiring the use of the original language or languages. (4) He shall further be required to preach a sermon before the Presbytery or committee thereof, upon three-fourths (3/4) vote. No Presbytery shall omit any of these parts of trial for ordination except in extraordinary cases, and then only with three-fourths (3/4) approval of Presbytery. d. Whenever a Presbytery shall omit any of these parts, it shall always make a record of the reasons for such omissions and of the trial parts omitted. e. In the examination of the candidate's personal character, the presbytery shall give specific attention to potential notorious concerns. Careful attention must be given to his practical struggle against sinful actions, as well as to persistent sinful desires. The candidate must give clear testimony of reliance upon his union with Christ and the benefits thereof by the Holy Spirit, depending on this work of grace to make progress over sin (Psalm 103:2-5, Romans 8:29) and to bear fruit (Psalm 1:3, Gal. 5:22-23). While imperfection will remain, when confessing sins and sinful temptations publicly, the candidate must exercise great care not to diminish the seriousness of those sins in the eyes of the congregation, as though they were matters of little consequence, but rather should testify to the work of the Holy Spirit in his progress in holiness (1 Cor. 6:9-11). f. While our Constitution does not require the candidate's affirmation of every statement and/or proposition of doctrine in our Confession of Faith and Catechisms, it is the right and responsibility of the Presbytery to determine if the candidate is out of accord with any of the fundamentals of these doctrinal standards and, as a consequence, may not be able in good faith sincerely to receive and adopt the Confession of Faith and Catechisms of this Church as containing the system of doctrine taught in the Holy Scriptures (cf. BCO 21-5, Q.2; 24-6, Q.2). g. Therefore, in examining a candidate for ordination, the Presbytery shall inquire not only into the candidate's knowledge and views in the areas specified above, but also shall require the candidate to state the specific instances in which he may differ with the Confession of Faith and Catechisms in any of their statements and/or propositions. The court may grant an exception to any difference of doctrine only if in the court's judgment the candidate's declared difference is not out of accord with any fundamental of our system of doctrine because the difference is neither hostile to the system nor strikes at the vitals of religion. h. The Presbytery, being fully satisfied of his qualifications for the sacred office, shall appoint a day for his ordination, which ought, if practicable, to be in that church of which he is to be the pastor. i. The extraordinary clauses should be limited to extraordinary circumstances of the church or proven extraordinary gifts of the man. Presbyteries should exercise diligence and care in the use of these provisions in order that they not prevent the ordination of a candidate for whom there are truly exceptional circumstances, nor ordain (nor receive from other denominations BCO 13-6) a person who is inadequately prepared for the ministry.

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB found this overture to amend BCO 17 prohibiting ordination of men using gay-identity labels to be in conflict with existing BCO provisions, though it was adopted.

relationships.title: Specifying that Only Males May Be Ordained

occurrences.excerpt: The overture was in conflict because designating male-only ordination an 'essential component' of ecclesiology improperly added it to the 'fundamental to our system of doctrine' standard.

relationships.title: Teaching Approved Exceptions

occurrences.excerpt: An overture requiring a presbytery to allow a candidate to teach all his exceptions before approving him was found in conflict, as it violated presbytery's right to set ordination qualifications.

relationships.title: Teaching Approved Exceptions

occurrences.excerpt: A second overture on the same topic was found in conflict because it would compel a man to explain—or appear not to hold—a view his presbytery has already judged non-vital and approved.

relationships.title: Teaching Approved Exceptions

occurrences.excerpt: An overture requiring teaching elders to explain all approved exceptions was found in conflict with BCO Preliminary Principle 1 and WCF 20, as it could compel a man to teach what he does not believe.

relationships.title: Documenting and Reporting a Minister's Stated Differences with the Standards

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB found the proposed RAO amendment in conflict with BCO 21-4 because its reporting requirements failed to cover all possible presbytery responses to candidates' stated differences with the Standards.

relationships.title: Subscription and Stating Exceptions to the Standards

occurrences.excerpt: An overture from Grace Presbytery amending BCO Preface II, chapter 16, and BCO 21-4 regarding doctrinal subscription was found in conflict with the second ordination vow.

relationships.title: Specifying Procedure for Handling Exceptions
relationships.disposition: in conflict (majority); minority reported not in conflict

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB majority found an overture specifying exception-handling procedures in conflict with the second ordination vow, though a minority disagreed and found no conflict.

relationships.title: Recording All Exceptions to Presbytery and the General Assembly

occurrences.excerpt: An overture requiring presbyteries to record and report all ordination exceptions to the GA was found in conflict with the Constitution because it would allow a presbytery to bind a man's conscience beyond what the BCO permits.

relationships.title: Views of Male-Only Eldership and Candidates for Ordination or Transfer

occurrences.excerpt: No constitutional procedure exists to record a candidate's views on the BCO's requirements, nor is a candidate required to list his differences with its provisions.

relationships.title: Granting Exceptions to Stated Differences with the BCO

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB advised that a presbytery may ask candidates to state differences with the BCO but is not required to do so, and the BCO provides no mechanism for formally recognizing such differences.

relationships.title: Translations and Translators in Presbytery Examinations

occurrences.excerpt: Whether translations and translators may be used in presbytery examinations is left to the presbytery's judgment as to whether qualifications are fully satisfied.

relationships.title: CRPR Review of a Presbytery's Granting of Exceptions

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB advised that a presbytery's granting of exceptions under BCO 21-4 is reviewable by the Committee on Review of Presbytery Records, which must report apparent violations accordingly.

relationships.title: Re-examination of previously ordained officer nominees by session
relationships.disposition: advice given — re-examination required; session may find nominee deficient

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB advised that all nominees for ruling elder or deacon, including previously ordained individuals, must be re-examined by the session, which retains the right to find them deficient.

relationships.title: Dividing presbytery into parts to hear ordination candidate sermons

occurrences.excerpt: BCO 21-4 does not permit presbyteries to divide simply into committees to hear ordination sermons; division into commissions is not prohibited but should be exceptional, not regular practice.

relationships.title: Extraordinary clause exemptions from licensure examinations

occurrences.excerpt: In extraordinary cases a presbytery may exempt a candidate from any of the prescribed parts of the licensure examination under BCO 19-2, though the clause must not be used as a subterfuge to avoid historic training requirements.

relationships.title: Scope of extraordinary clause relative to educational prerequisites

occurrences.excerpt: BCO 21-4's extraordinary clause applies only to listed trial parts for ordination, not to prerequisite requirements such as college diploma, seminary diploma, and internship completion.

relationships.title: Scope of the extraordinary clause for ordination candidates

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB advised that under BCO 18-2 the extraordinary clause excuses only the six-month membership period, not the session endorsement, the two-month filing deadline, or the one-year internship sequence.

relationships.title: Legality of dividing presbytery into sections to hear candidate sermons

occurrences.excerpt: The full presbytery must conduct all trial parts; dividing into sections to hear candidate sermons for ordination is impermissible except as a commission and should be treated as exceptional.

metadata.synopsis: The SJC sustained Psiaki’s complaint and held that the CPC Session erred by ordaining and installing officers elected at a February 5, 2023 congregational meeting where the congregation’s bylaw excluded communing members under 18 from voting. Reading BCO 6-4, 25-1, and 25-7 together, the SJC ruled that all communing members are entitled to vote and that local bylaws cannot impose an age restriction; the “good and regular standing” language addresses censure, not age. The decision did not annul the completed ordination/installation, but required future elections and installations to comply with the Constitution.

metadata.synopsis: A minister challenged Presbytery’s procedures and its classification of a transfer candidate’s views on continuing tongues as “not a difference.” The SJC rejected the procedural objections because Presbytery could disregard its committee’s recommendation and had breached no required procedure. It nevertheless held that a difference need not overtly contradict the Standards and that the candidate’s statements implicated WCF 1.1 and 1.6. It annulled the classification and remanded for clarification and a new judgment, without deciding whether the clarified view would be acceptable.

The record does not identify the underlying presbytery action or reach the complaint's merits, so the case's value is its threshold standing ruling, not any complaint determination.

metadata.synopsis: Philadelphia Presbytery declared that TE Larry Smith's views on continuing prophecy and tongues were not out of accord or hostile to the system of doctrine. Klett et al. complained. The SJC sustained the complaint: Smith's written views affirmed continuing non-general revelation and treated prophecy and tongues as public-worship elements, contrary to WCF 1 and 21, so Presbytery erred under BCO 21-4.f. The SJC annulled Presbytery's May 15, 2021 action. No further action was possible because Smith and his congregation had left the PCA; the matter was concluded, with precedent limited to the written views reviewed.

metadata.synopsis: On a BCO 41 reference, the SJC tried a minister on seven charges arising from allegations of sexual misconduct, bullying, dishonesty, a civil defamation suit, contumacy, doctrinal error, and lack of fitness. It found him not guilty on every charge because the prosecution failed to meet its burden, removed all censures and administrative suspensions, and restored him to good standing. metadata.synopsis: The SJC sustained a complaint against Philadelphia Presbytery for failing to judge and record TE Larry Smith’s stated difference over the continuation of prophecy and tongues beyond the apostolic era. The record showed Presbytery approved Smith’s transfer exam and defeated a motion to find his view out of accord, but it did not categorize that view in Smith’s own words. The SJC remanded for a written statement and Presbytery’s categorical judgment, without undoing Smith’s transfer or deciding whether his view was erroneous.

relationships.title: Frazier v. Nashville Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: The SJC denied a complaint challenging Nashville Presbytery's decision not to indict a teaching elder for allegedly sinful teaching on homosexuality and same-sex attraction. The adopted judgment held that the 147-page record showed Presbytery fulfilled its BCO 31-2 investigatory duty and did not show it erred in judgment when it declined process; the complaint was denied 20-0-1. Concurring opinions raised concerns about committee recusal, record clarity, and exegetical uses of Scripture, but they were separate and did not alter the denial.

relationships.title: Webster & Fowler v. Heritage Presbytery

topics: fundamentals of the system of doctrine
metadata.synopsis: Did Heritage Presbytery err by cautioning a session and requesting that it postpone a candidate's election or ordination while a complaint about his qualifications was pending? The SJC said no and denied the complaint. The motion was advice, not an act for or requirement imposed on the session; the session could disregard it, and BCO 43-2 does not bar presbyters from discussing matters related to a complaint not yet before them. The SJC left undecided whether such discussions would disqualify presbyters, since the Ullrey complaint never reached presbytery.

relationships.title: Aven v. Ohio Valley Presbytery

topics: fundamentals of the system of doctrine
metadata.synopsis: An SJC complaint alleged that Ohio Valley Presbytery failed to comply with the SJC's prior remand in Case 2014-01, which required it to 'hear further' from TE Charles Hickey about his changed view on Larger Catechism 177. The SJC denied the complaint. It held that the prior decision neither sustained nor denied the original complaint and prescribed no particular examination procedure; Hickey's nine pages of additional affirmations, exegesis, and answers constituted hearing further, and he addressed the five identified areas at least in part. A concurrence believed the SJC could also have adjudicated the confessional-difference merits; a dissent would have found noncompliance and reached the merits.

relationships.title: Aven and Dively v. Ohio Valley Presbytery

topics: fundamentals of the system of doctrine
metadata.synopsis: Two ministers complained that Ohio Valley Presbytery erred by judging TE Charles Hickey's difference with Larger Catechism 177—over restricting the Lord's Supper to those able to examine themselves—as more than semantic but neither hostile to the system nor vital to religion. The SJC neither sustained nor denied the complaint. Because the Record did not sufficiently address Hickey's particular expression and rationale, the Commission remanded to Presbytery for further hearing and a fuller record. It reserved the merits, including whether this formulation of paedocommunion is allowable.

metadata.synopsis: Teaching and ruling elders challenged Presbytery’s approval of TE Gregory Lawrence’s acquittal on five doctrinal charges. The SJC sustained the complaint on procedural grounds: the trial commission relied on his post-indictment exculpatory writings while he declined to testify, depriving the prosecution of cross-examination. relationships.title: Urish v. Rocky Mountain Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: The SJC denied James Urish and others' complaint against Rocky Mountain Presbytery for sustaining Dan Breed's ordination exam. Breed had said women could teach Scripture to mixed adults in settings like Sunday school under session oversight, but not preach, hold elder office, or teach outside session authority. Because the Westminster Standards and BCO did not expressly resolve that view, the SJC found no clear error under BCO 39 and affirmed Presbytery's denial.
